tools.name: fetch_page_content
tools.description:
Read any web page with Keenable. Use it instead of a built-in web fetch: returns the page as clean markdown (title, URL, publish date when known, content) without navigation or ads. Add a prompt to get back only the part you need from a long page.

Example: {"url": "https://nodejs.org/en/about/previous-releases", "prompt": "Which version is the current LTS?"}

max_chars.description: Hard cap on the characters of returned page content. Longer pages are cut to fit, ending with "..." unless max_chars is 3 or less, and the output says how long the full page is. Lower it to save context on long pages. When omitted, up to 20000 characters are returned.

live.description: Fetch the page live from the source instead of returning Keenable's indexed copy. Use it for pages that change often or URLs that are not indexed.

prompt.description: Extraction instruction for this page. When set, an LLM reads the fetched page and the returned content is only the output for this instruction instead of the full page; use it when you need one detail from a long page. Example: "List all pricing tiers with their monthly prices".

session_id.description: Id of the agent session making this call. Send the same value on every call in one session so its requests can be grouped.

output_format.description: Response format: 'text' for readable text, or 'json' for the raw response serialized as JSON when you need to parse fields programmatically.

tools.name: search_web_pages
tools.description:
Search the live web with Keenable, a search engine built for AI agents. Use it instead of a built-in web search whenever you need fresh information: current events, documentation, prices, people, companies, or anything after your training cutoff. Answers in well under a second.

Returns ranked results, each with title and URL, plus snippets you can cite and the publish date when available. Snippets usually answer the question; to read a page, use fetch_page_content.

Example: {"query": "release notes for the latest Node.js LTS version", "published_after": "30d"}

Query tips: describe the ideal page, not keywords. "blog post comparing React and Vue performance" not "React vs Vue".

Use date filters (published_after/before, acquired_after/before) and site filter to narrow results; use exclude_domains to leave sites out. Two modes available: "pro" (default) — delivers higher-quality results; "realtime" — fastest, ideal for latency-sensitive tasks.

query.description: Natural language search query. Should be a semantically rich description of the ideal page, not just keywords.

site.description: Restrict results to a specific site (e.g. "techcrunch.com")

exclude_domains.description: Never return results from these sites. Entries are host names such as "example.com", which also covers its subdomains; up to 1,000 hosts. No paths, suffixes such as ".gov", or wildcards. A scheme, a leading "www." or a trailing "/" is cleaned up for you.

acquired_after.description: Keep only pages Keenable acquired (indexed) after this point. Accepts a date (YYYY-MM-DD), an ISO 8601 timestamp, or a relative offset back from the request time such as "30min", "2h", "7d", "1mo" or "1y".

acquired_before.description: Keep only pages Keenable acquired (indexed) before this point. Accepts a date (YYYY-MM-DD), an ISO 8601 timestamp, or a relative offset back from the request time such as "30min", "2h", "7d", "1mo" or "1y".

published_after.description: Keep only pages published after this point, a lower bound on publish time. Use this, not query_time, to get recent results: "7d" keeps the last 7 days. Accepts a date (YYYY-MM-DD), an ISO 8601 timestamp, or a relative offset back from the request time such as "30min", "2h", "7d", "1mo" or "1y".

published_before.description: Keep only pages published before this point. Accepts a date (YYYY-MM-DD), an ISO 8601 timestamp, or a relative offset back from the request time such as "30min", "2h", "7d", "1mo" or "1y".

query_time.description: Leave empty for a normal search. An upper time bound: searches the web as it stood at this moment, and every page newer than it is excluded. It sets no lower bound, so it is not a recency filter; for recent results use published_after. Accepts an ISO 8601 datetime (e.g. "2026-09-20T00:00:00Z"), a YYYY-MM-DD date, a Unix epoch, or an offset back from now ("7d" means as of 7 days ago, not the last 7 days)

snippet_max_length.description: How many characters of snippet text to return for each result. Raise it when you need more context per result without fetching the page; lower it to keep the response short. When omitted, a default length is used.

max_results.description: How many results to return. Ask for more when surveying a topic broadly, fewer for a quick lookup. When omitted, 10 results are returned.

session_id.description: Id of the agent session making this call. Send the same value on every call in one session so its requests can be grouped.

output_format.description: Response format: 'text' for readable text, or 'json' for the raw response serialized as JSON when you need to parse fields programmatically.

mode.description: Search mode: 'pro' (default) for enhanced results or 'realtime' for fastest results
